value.body: An economic analyst studies economic data and trends, such as growth, inflation, trade and markets, to inform decisions in companies, banks, research bodies or government. Employers include banks, research and rating agencies, consulting firms, think tanks and government departments. A typical day involves collecting and analysing data, building simple models, and writing reports or briefs.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.A./B.Sc Economics; an M.A. in Economics is common

items.label: Government route
items.value: Indian Economic Service via the UPSC IES/ISS exam

items.label: Indian Economic Service vacancies
items.note: 12 IES vacancies were notified in the 2025 exam; numbers are provisional

items.label: IES entry pay level
items.note: Junior Time Scale; allowances are extra

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Most roles prefer a master's in economics; freshers often start as research assistants at think tanks, research firms or bank research teams. Government roles come through the UPSC IES exam or RBI and other regulator recruitment.

value.title: At a glance
items: A bachelor's alone usually leads to research assistant or data roles.
Next roles: economist, senior research analyst, policy analyst.
Research roles value writing and published work.
